original_question: Let S = C[x0, ..., xn], let f be a homogeneous polynomial of degree d whose hypersurface V(f) in projective space P^n is smooth, let J_f be the Jacobian ideal generated by the partial derivatives of f, and let M(f) = S/J_f be the graded Milnor or Jacobian algebra. Does M(f) always have the weak Lefschetz property, and does it perhaps always have the strong Lefschetz property?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it uses the correct ambient ring S=\mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_n], the correct object f (a homogeneous polynomial of degree d), the smooth projective hypersurface V(f)\subset \mathbb{P}^n, the correct Jacobian ideal J_f generated by the partial derivatives, the Milnor/Jacobian algebra M(f)=S/J_f, and it asks exactly about the weak and strong Lefschetz properties for this algebra.
missing_details: The paper’s exact target is an open question in Section 2 (“Jacobian ideals”), labeled Question 2.8; it is not presented there as a conjecture or theorem.

To make the question fully stand-alone, WLP should be defined: there exists a linear form L\in M(f)_1 (equivalently, the class of a linear form in S_1) such that the multiplication maps \times L\colon M(f)_i\to M(f)_{i+1} have maximal rank for every i.
Likewise, SLP should be defined: there exists a linear form L\in M(f)_1 such that for every m\ge 1 and every i, the maps \times L^m\colon M(f)_i\to M(f)_{i+m} have maximal rank.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the question ranges over every n and every homogeneous form f\in \mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_n] with smooth V(f)\subset \mathbb{P}^n.
The paper does not impose any additional degree restriction in the formal question itself, even though the immediately preceding context records known cases.
No separate nilpotency hypothesis appears in the paper’s formulation; the relevant algebra is simply the graded Milnor/Jacobian algebra attached to a smooth projective hypersurface.

For paper-faithfulness, it is worth noting the nearby motivating context: generic f is known to give both WLP and SLP, and WLP is known for f\in \mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_3] of degree d\le 6 with smooth V(f).
refined_question: Let S=\mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_n], let f\in S be a homogeneous polynomial of degree d, and assume that the projective hypersurface V(f)=\{x\in \mathbb{P}^n\mid f(x)=0\} is smooth. Let J_f=(\partial f/\partial x_0,\dots,\partial f/\partial x_n) and let M(f)=S/J_f be the graded Milnor (Jacobian) algebra. Is it true that for every such f, the algebra M(f) has the weak Lefschetz property, i.e. there exists a linear form L\in M(f)_1 such that \times L\colon M(f)_i\to M(f)_{i+1} has maximal rank for all i? More strongly, must M(f) always have the strong Lefschetz property, i.e. does there exist L\in M(f)_1 such that \times L^m\colon M(f)_i\to M(f)_{i+m} has maximal rank for all i and all m\ge 1?
justification: The draft does not target any Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 in this paper, because arXiv:2311.03081 is a problem list and the matching item is instead Section 2, Question 2.8. Section 2 first sets the standing assumption of characteristic zero, and the Jacobian-ideals paragraph then specializes to S=\mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_n], homogeneous f of degree d, smooth V(f)\subset \mathbb{P}^n, J_f generated by the partial derivatives, and M(f)=S/J_f. The official formulation is exactly: whether M(f) has the WLP (or the SLP) for any homogeneous form f with smooth V(f). The same paragraph supplies the paper-specific scope and motivation: generic f is known to give both WLP and SLP, and WLP is already known for f\in \mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_3] of degree d\le 6 with smooth V(f).
